notes: Current registered control. Absence of a distinct pollinating anther is source-secure and the 2021 plastome tree places M. australasica sister to the sampled remainder of Monochoria. Direct species-level pollination evidence and exclusion of alternatively sampled nonheterantherous congeners remain open.

PlantNET describes the six stamens as more or less equal, supporting absence of the case-defining heteranthery. M. cyanea is represented in the 2018 total-evidence phylogeny but absent from the 2021 plastome sample used for the incumbent-control receipt. Direct flower-visitation evidence and a common-tree proximity comparison remain unresolved.

Current registered shared control. Heteranthery absence and placement in the sampled plastome topology are source-secure; direct species-level pollination evidence and closest-eligible closure remain open.
Alternative equal-stamen congener that must be included in the closest-control search. Direct pollination evidence and relative phylogenetic proximity remain unresolved, so it is not promoted.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Luo et al. 2009 code long and short stamen sets and include S. surattensis among heteromorphic-stamen species.

Rejected after primary-morphology audit. Irwin and Barneby describe three long and four short fertile stamens with different anther dimensions. A later comparative table labelled the species non-heterantherous, but the frozen U3 definition follows the directly described discrete fertile-stamen sets.

S. siamea is phylogenetically close in a recent plastome comparison, but morphology divides its seven fertile stamens into two long and five short sets; Luo et al. also code multiple stamen classes. Close proximity cannot rescue the negative-control gate.

S. martiana is a sampled clade-II taxon, but direct Irwin-Barneby morphology shows strongly differentiated fertile stamens: four median anthers are small/mostly sterile while two large latero-abaxial fertile anthers are 8-14 mm. Same-clade proximity cannot make it an absence control.

S. pleurocarpa is a sampled clade-II taxon, but the NSW flora explicitly distinguishes two largest anthers around 9 mm from the remaining fertile stamens. It therefore fails the binary heteranthery-absence gate.

Direct morphology distinguishes two fertile stamens with anthers around 10 mm from five fertile stamens around 5 mm. The species is therefore a same-clade heterantherous comparison, not a negative control.
Direct morphology separates two long latero-abaxial anthers from the shorter median/centric fertile anthers. The same-clade candidate fails the absence gate.
Direct morphology records two long abaxial stamens with 10.5-18 mm anthers. This sampled clade-II species therefore fails the heteranthery-absence gate.

S. paradictyon is a sampled clade-II taxon. The comparative anther study states that the two lateral long abaxial anthers are characteristic of clade II and explicitly includes S. paradictyon in that morphology, with specialized elongated abaxial anther tips. This directly violates the frozen binary heteranthery-absence criterion, closing the last unresolved sampled clade-II candidate as a rejection.

Irwin and Barneby describe seven fertile anthers as isomorphic, so the heteranthery-absence gate passes. However the Senna phylogenetic framework places S. atomaria in clade III while S. alata is in clade II. A cross-clade jump cannot be called the closest eligible comparison while clade-II candidates remain under adjudication. The candidate is therefore rejected on proximity rather than retained merely because its morphology is convenient.

Species descriptions give seven fertile stamens with anthers of approximately equal length around 5 mm, supporting the frozen heteranthery-absence criterion. A 2024 reproductive-biology study identifies a cross-pollinating system with Tetragonula as the major visitor and Xylocopa as a regular visitor, so animal-pollination eligibility passes. Available plastome evidence places S. spectabilis with S. obtusifolia/S. tora/S. occidentalis but does not resolve its relative distance to S. alata on a common candidate tree; proximity and closest-eligible status therefore remain open.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Weaker differentiation than the case does not establish heteranthery absence.
Rejected after primary-morphology audit. Three long and four short fertile stamens violate the frozen absence criterion even though a later synthesis called the species non-heterantherous.

Recent ITS evidence recovers S. corymbosa and S. bicapsularis as sister taxa, closing the closest-relative search for this candidate, but direct floral work describes differentiated stamen functions. Sister status cannot override failure of the outcome-absence gate.

The case lies in heterantherous VIIa and S. armata lies in the sister VIIb lineage, so morphology and phylogenetic grain are acceptable. However direct effective-pollination evidence remains weaker than for the equally grained VIIb candidate S. covesii. Under the preregistered tie-break, source quality therefore rejects S. armata as the primary replacement rather than leaving multiple convenient VIIb choices open.

S. bauhinioides is a sampled VIIb species, but direct monographic morphology differentiates the seven fertile stamens into shortest, intermediate and longest positions. The same monograph identifies floral traits as signs of autogamy. It therefore fails both the strict heteranthery-absence criterion and the animal-pollination eligibility gate.

S. villosa is a sampled VIIb species, but the direct species description distinguishes four median stamens with straighter shorter anthers from three abaxial stamens with longer more incurved anthers. The differentiation is modest but discrete, so it fails the frozen binary heteranthery-absence gate.

S. covesii is explicitly placed in VIIb, the sister subclade to the case's VIIa, whose fertile stamens are more or less the same length and shape. Species-level sources describe seven fertile stamens, and Marazzi directly reports small bees buzzing its flowers. S. armata occupies the same phylogenetic grain but lacks comparably strong direct pollination evidence, so the preregistered SOURCE_QUALITY tie-break selects S. covesii as the screened replacement candidate.
